claims.kb_note: Revised 2026-10-20: narrowed from 'LDLJ is not a valid cross-dataset comparator when control modes or control frequencies differ significantly (> ~2x)'. Two matched-rate comparisons rank position smoother than velocity (the expected order), so the control-mode half was dropped; the sampling-rate half stands (eval/investigations/ldlj/SUBSAMPLING.md).
claims.assertion: LDLJ is not a valid cross-dataset comparator when sampling rates differ significantly (> ~2x); at a matched rate, control mode alone does not break comparability
claims.conditions: Tested with ldlj_definition per_submovement_v1 by changing only the sampling rate of the same trajectories, and across datasets at native rates (eval/investigations/ldlj/SUBSAMPLING.md). The whole-episode evidence (Calibra <= 0.12) and the 2026-10-19 single-dataset measurements are retracted below. Revised 2026-10-20: the control-mode half of the assertion was dropped after two matched-rate tests.

evidence.notes: Only the sampling rate changes (every k-th step kept; gripper_dims [6, 13]). LDLJ moves 5.1 units and crosses from WARNING to OK. eval/investigations/ldlj/SUBSAMPLING.md.

Same test on sim human teleop. Subsampled to 10 Hz it scores like lerobot/pusht at its native 10 Hz (-8.89), so the PushT-vs-ALOHA gap is explained by sampling rate. eval/investigations/ldlj/SUBSAMPLING.md.

evidence.dataset: nvidia/BridgeData2_LeRobot_v3 (5 Hz, velocity) vs lerobot/aloha_* (50 Hz, position)
evidence.notes: Different control mode and a 10x rate gap: the velocity-command dataset scores smoother than every position-command ALOHA dataset, the physically unexpected order. BridgeData2 measured on revision b96f7216 from its data/ and meta/ files (velocity mode, last dim excluded), matching calibra/references/bridgedata_v2.json as re-profiled 2026-10-20. eval/investigations/ldlj/SUBSAMPLING.md.

evidence.dataset: lerobot/pusht (sim, position) vs lerobot/columbia_cairlab_pusht_real (real, velocity), both 10 Hz
evidence.notes: Same task (PushT), same native rate, different control mode: position scores smoother, the physically expected order, with non-overlapping CIs. cairlab actions correlate 1.00 with the next state change. Confound: sim vs real hardware. eval/investigations/ldlj/control_mode.py.

evidence.dataset: nvidia/BridgeData2_LeRobot_v3 (velocity) vs lerobot/aloha_* subsampled (position), both 5 Hz
evidence.notes: Different tasks and hardware, matched 5 Hz: position scores smoother, the expected order. eval/investigations/ldlj/SUBSAMPLING.md.

falsification.condition: Two datasets more than 2x apart in sampling rate that LDLJ ranks in the physically expected order, OR two datasets of different control mode at a matched rate that it ranks in the unexpected order

retracted_evidence.notes: DROID, 7-DOF position-command, 15Hz, 100 episodes of real hardware teleoperation. LDLJ −19.39 at 15Hz vs aloha −20.43 at 50Hz — a gap of only 1.0 unit despite 3.3× frequency difference. Within same control mode, frequency has limited LDLJ impact. Contrast with cross-mode gap: pusht (velocity) −16.34 vs aloha (position) −20.43 = 4.1 units gap despite a smaller frequency difference. Confirms that the control-mode dimension dominates over frequency for LDLJ divergence. Resolves pending test for 'low-frequency position-command dataset'. [Corrected 2026-09-27: pusht is position control, so the pusht-vs-aloha gap is within-mode at a 5x frequency difference. The conclusion that control mode dominates frequency is not supported by this pair.]

retracted_evidence.notes: BridgeData V2, 7-DOF velocity-command, 5Hz. LDLJ −13.79 vs pusht (velocity, 10Hz) at −16.34 — a 2.55-unit gap within the same control mode at 2x frequency difference. Cross-mode gap (velocity vs position): pusht −16.34 vs aloha −20.43 = 4.1 units. Shows that both frequency AND control mode contribute to LDLJ divergence. Further supports LDLJ-001: LDLJ is not a valid cross-dataset comparator even within the same control mode when frequencies differ ≥2x. [Corrected 2026-09-27: pusht is position control, so BridgeData2 vs pusht crosses control mode and frequency; the 'within the same control mode' reading does not hold. The entry still supports LDLJ-001 as a cross-mode, cross-frequency divergence.]

claims.assertion: LDLJ may be valid for within-type comparison (same control mode, similar frequency)
claims.conditions: control frequencies within ~2x, same action space semantics. Tested with ldlj_definition per_submovement_v1 against known-worse (spike-injected) copies; see eval/investigations/ldlj/SPIKE_INJECTION.md. The whole-episode evidence (Calibra <= 0.12) and the 2026-10-19 single-dataset measurements are retracted below.

evidence.notes: Known-worse copy from `calibra corrupt lerobot/aloha_static_battery --inject-spikes 0.02` (seed 42; see eval/investigations/ldlj/SPIKE_INJECTION.md). LDLJ does not fall on the corrupted copy (it rises or stays flat), so it fails to distinguish known-worse from clean within the same type, which is this claim's falsification condition. Jerk spike rate detects every run.

falsification.note: Falsified 2026-10-19 by spike injection on ALOHA (real and sim) and SO-100: per-sub-movement LDLJ scores the corrupted copy as smoother or unchanged in 5 of 6 runs (eval/investigations/ldlj/SPIKE_INJECTION.md). Injector-dependent: with adjacent-step swaps and per-episode MAD outliers (experiments/results/benign_firing_rates.md, rerun 2026-10-20) ldlj catches 6 of 7 corrupted aloha_sim_insertion_scripted episodes (with the aloha profile; 5 of 7 without) but 0 of 30 on PushT. A successor claim should state which corruption types and detection mode it covers, and be tested with noise-type corruption too.

retracted_evidence.notes: Velocity-command 2D sim, ~10Hz, 206 episodes, image-conditioned demonstrations. LDLJ −16.01, consistent with pusht_velocity_command (−16.34). First of two matched velocity-command datasets for within-type comparison.
retracted_evidence.retraction_reason: lerobot/pusht_image has the same actions as lerobot/pusht; its old reference scored only the x axis in float32. Profiled correctly it matches pusht exactly, so it is not a second dataset.

retracted_evidence.notes: Velocity-command 2D sim, ~10Hz, 206 episodes. LDLJ −16.34. Second of two matched velocity-command datasets. Gap to pusht_image: only 0.33 units. Both datasets same control mode and frequency — LDLJ agrees to within 2%, supporting LDLJ's validity for within-type comparison. Resolves pending test 'Two velocity-command datasets with different operator quality'. Caveat: pusht_image and pusht are variants of the same task, not truly independent; evidence strength upgrades from zero to LOW-MODERATE only.
retracted_evidence.retraction_reason: Its support was the match with lerobot/pusht_image, which is the same data.

retracted_evidence.notes: BridgeData V2 (velocity, 5Hz) LDLJ −13.79 vs pusht (velocity, 10Hz) −16.34 = 2.55-unit gap within the same control class. LDLJ-002 asserts within-type comparison is valid 'at similar frequency'. BridgeData2 shows that even a 2x frequency difference within velocity-command datasets produces a meaningful LDLJ divergence. This partially challenges LDLJ-002: within-type validity requires frequency matching (≤2x), not just the same control class. The condition 'similar frequency' in LDLJ-002 is validated rather than falsified — the claim's frequency qualifier is confirmed necessary.
retracted_evidence.retraction_reason: Compares a 5 Hz velocity-command dataset with lerobot/pusht, which is position control, not velocity. The comparison crosses control mode and frequency at once, so it cannot isolate either.
